# 瑜伽師地論分門記

**ID:** T2801
**Volume:** T85

**Original Category:** 古逸部
**Byline:** 唐 法成撰．智慧山記
**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 618–907
**Juans:** 6

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A six-fascicle Dūnhuáng manuscript text in which the East-Tibetan / Hexi-corridor master [法成](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E6%88%90) (Chos-grub, fl. early-to-mid 9th c.) lectured on the structure of the *Yúqié shī dì lùn* ([KR6n0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0001)), with his lectures recorded by his disciple [智慧山](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%85%A7%E5%B1%B1) (Prajñāparvata). The "fēnmén" 分門 ("dividing the sections") title indicates that the work is a topical-structural commentary, providing a formal subdivision of the 100 *juǎn* of the master treatise rather than a lemma-by-lemma gloss. It is preserved only in Dūnhuáng manuscripts (Pelliot Chinois 2061 and related fragments) and was first edited into the modern canon as Taishō No. 2801 in vol. 85 (the Dūnhuáng-text volume).

**Abstract**

[法成](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E6%88%90) (Tib. *Chos-grub*) was the most important Sino-Tibetan-bilingual Buddhist scholar of the late Tang, active at the Yúlín 榆林 and Mògāo 莫高 cave-temples of Dūnhuáng during the period of Tibetan rule and after the Zhāng Yìcháo 張議潮 restoration in 848. His lecture-translation of the *Yogācārabhūmi* and other Yogācāra treatises into Tibetan is the principal route by which Cí'ēn-doctrine reached Tibetan Buddhism; conversely, his lecture-records in Chinese — preserved at Dūnhuáng — are major witnesses to the late-Tang scholastic reception of [窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA)'s tradition outside Cháng'ān itself. The composition window adopted here (833–865) brackets his most active teaching period, attested in the Dūnhuáng manuscripts.

T2801 and the parallel [KR6n0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0010) *Yúqié lùn shǒu jì* 瑜伽論手記 (T85n2802) — recorded by [福慧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A6%8F%E6%85%A7) — represent two streams of [法成](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E6%88%90)'s teaching activity. T2801 in particular preserves Fǎchéng's scheme for subdividing the 100 *juǎn* into intelligible study-units, a project of considerable practical value for monastic curricula.
